name: @thetis/tool-operator
description: The operator's own tool: one tool that asks this Thetis server to restart itself, refused while an update is installing. Installed per admin, never for everyone. The restart countdown everyone sees is gateway-web's.

tools.name: restart_daemon
tools.description: Ask this Thetis server to restart itself. A restart is only for what Thetis reads once when it starts: the runtime modules in src/, the thetis command, and the `door` and `storage` settings. Extension updates apply by themselves, and other settings without a restart. This call only records the request. Running replies, this one included, then pause at their next safe point; Thetis counts down where everyone can see it, restarts, and the paused replies continue by themselves when it is back, so nobody has to type "continue". A reply still inside a long tool call two minutes later is stopped there and saved, and continues the same way. Open terminal shell sessions do not come back, and whatever was running in one dies with them. While an update is installing this is refused: the update restarts Thetis itself when it is done. Ask the person with ask_user before you call this, unless they have just asked for it. The reason must name what changed; it is shown to everyone waiting and recorded. A refusal means nothing happened: say what it says, and do not call this again.

reason.description: What changed, and why only a restart picks it up. Shown to everyone waiting and recorded in the journal.
